newsitem.title: USA: Situation quiet in Northern Iraq - Pentagon.
newsitem.headline: Situation quiet in Northern Iraq - Pentagon.

text.p: The U.S. Defence Department on Thursday denied reports that Iraq's forces were again preparing to move against Kurds in northern Iraq and said the situation around the city of Arbil appeared to be quiet.
"We don't see it happening. We don't see any attacks or massing of tanks in the area between Arbil and Sulaimaniya," said Navy Lt. Cmdr. Scott Campbell, a Pentagon spokesman.
Campbell had been asked about reports that the Iraqi army appeared to be moving a large number of tanks in the region.

United Nations guards and foreign aid workers in northern Iraq said on Thursday that rival Kurdish factions had clashed near a strategic bridge at the village of Degala as Iraqi troops and armour stood by but did not intervene.
Their radio reports from the field, monitored in Arbil, said fighting was heavy between forces of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).

The PUK office in London said in a statement that 120 to 150 Iraqi tanks were in the area, heading in the direction of Koi Sanjaq. Heavy artillery and KDP fighters accompanied the tanks, the statement said.
